recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Do not restore Ingredient.description unless BR&R makes a new explicit decision reversing FHIR-31810 and redefining the excipient-list use case; the current build should retain the narrower Ingredient.comment element.
issue_request: FHIR-26568 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R R5 change request to add Ingredient.description as markdown so an Ingredient could carry uncoded textual ingredient or excipient text while Ingredient.role distinguished active, excipient, and similar categories.
initial_application: The change appears to have been initially applied in April 2020 by commit 5ddd37da99a21bdf1ea7c5ad0e7ffd0c5ef7d50f, whose subject says 'added Ingredient.description FHIR#26658'. That issue key appears to be a neighboring-key typo because the changed Ingredient spreadsheet and the BRR 2020-03-31 minutes match FHIR-26568's Ingredient.description request.
additional_context: FHIR-31810 was later Published/Persuasive for the same MedicinalProductIngredient/Ingredient artifact and resolved to drop Ingredient.description because a single Ingredient should not represent a list of other ingredients or excipients and there was no remaining use case. FHIR-28349 later accepted a narrower markdown note/comment use case and, after FHIR-I name review, the element was finalized as Ingredient.comment rather than Ingredient.description.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source has Ingredient.comment 0..1 markdown and no Ingredient.description, with Ingredient active in source/fhir.ini and MedicinalProductIngredient redirected to Ingredient. Restoring Ingredient.description for FHIR-26568 would contradict FHIR-31810 and confuse the later FHIR-28349 comment element.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive BR&R decision removed Ingredient.description and rejected the multiple-excipient-list use case.
Later Published/Persuasive with Modification decision added the surviving markdown notes capability as Ingredient.comment, not Ingredient.description.
